newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends little changed vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed little changed at 8.2919 on Tuesday from Monday's 8.2918 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai after Beijing announced an increase in China's foreign exchange reserves, traders said.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2918.
Beijing announced on Tuesday that China's foreign exchange reserves had hit a record of $117.6 billion by the end of May, up from $115 billion at the end of April.
Traders said the announcement had a positive but limited impact on the market and buying at 8.2920 saw the yuan move around current high levels.
The yuan opened slightly down at 8.2919 and moved in a narrow range between the intraday high of 8.2917 and 8.2920 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2930 late in trading.
Trading was dull with most business done at 8.2919, traders said.

One trader said despite the increase in foreign exchange reserves, the growth rate seemed to be slower than in the previous few months, indicating the People's Bank of China, the central bank, was buying fewer dollars.
"The central bank is expected to buy fewer dollars with what seems to be a smooth transition of Hong Kong to Chinese rule," he said.
"This will encourage the yuan's upward trend in the mid-term," he said.
Hong Kong became a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1, after 156 years as a British colony.
A second trader said buying at the 8.2920 level supported the yuan and that one deal right before the close, forcing the yuan down to an intraday low of 8.2930 would have no impact.
"The yuan is likely to rise slightly in the short term but move around the 8.2920 level on Wednesday," he said.
The yuan ended up at 7.3166 from 7.3653 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0717 from 1.0708 vs the Hong Kong dollar.
